My advice for home ownership:

1) Do not buy a house unless you plan to stay put for at least 7 years.

2) Buy the most expensive house you can afford on a fixed-rate 15-yr mortgage with 20% down.

I would advise buying a house instead of a condo, and a house without a HoA, but to each his own. (I would also suggest that you at least consider buying a duplex and renting the other side, depending on your handiness, industriousness, and tolerance for bullshit.)

The general rule of thumb for an affordable mortgage payment is 28% front end and 36% back end. By "payment" I mean PITI (Principle, Interest, Taxes, Insurance). Taxes are generally 1-1.5% of the home price annually. Likewise for insurance (i.e., A $100k house will typically pay $1000-1500 in taxes and a similar amount in insurance premiums every year).

FRONT END: Your mortgage payment should be no more than 28% of your total monthly income. If you earn $40k/yr ($3333/month) you should pay no more than $933 for PITI. Assuming Taxes and Insurance comprise 30% of your monthly payment, your Principle & Interest payments should be no more than $650. For a 15-year mortgage at 4%, you can safely borrow ~$88,000. With your 20% down payment of $22k (88k/.8 - 88k), you should be looking at houses for about $110-120k.

BACK END: Your total monthly debt payments should be no more than 36% of your total monthly income. Returning to the previous example, if you also have a $15,000 student loan balance at 6.8%, with corresponding payments of $172/month, that your total debt payments should be no more than $1200/month. $1200 - $172 = $1028, so you should be good with the above scenario. But if your student loan payments and car payments combine for $600/month, then your mortgage payment should be at most $1200 - $600 = $600. You can safely borrow ~$60k, and you should be looking at houses for about $75k with $15k down.
